item.title: Supply Chain and AI Threat Intelligence Platform - v1.2.3 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

New — Portfolio-Scale Analysis Visibility

Customers evaluating SCIP without a license key now see full analysis on their first 5 applications, with clear, real-time visibility into how many more applications are in their environment. Ingestion is never limited — every application you monitor is fully ingested and searchable regardless of scale. Analysis coverage beyond the first 5 unlocks with any paid license.

If your environment has more than 5 distinct applications, you'll see exactly how many are currently analyzed and how many aren't, everywhere that figure appears — dashboards, the Executive Summary, and a downloadable summary you can share internally to evaluate licensing options. See upgrade.html for tier details.

Fixed — scipingest Documentation Could Cause Silently Unindexed Data

The scipingest command's documented usage pattern could result in ingested SBOM data landing with a generic default sourcetype rather than the one SCIP's analysis searches read — meaning data indexed successfully, with no error, but never appeared in any dashboard or report. This affected any custom ingestion pipeline built using the documented example, for both CycloneDX and SPDX input.

The documentation has been corrected with the proper usage pattern. If you've built a custom ingestion pipeline using scipingest, verify your data is indexing with sourcetype=cyclonedx:component — search | eventcount summarize=false index=sbom_inventory and confirm the sourcetype breakdown matches what you expect, or update your pipeline to match the corrected example in the command's documentation.

item.title: SailPoint Adaptive Response - v3.0.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
As of version 3.0.0, this add-on is built on the official Splunk UCC Framework, ensuring long-term compatibility, enhanced security, and seamless operation within Splunk Cloud and Enterprise architectures. * Framework Migration * Migrated the Add-on to the **Splunk Unified Configuration Console (UCC)** framework. * Compatibility * Optimized for Splunk Enterprise and Splunk Cloud environments running Python 3.9+. * Tested On: Splunk Enterprise 10.4 (running Python 3.13) * Supported Splunk Platforms: * Splunk Cloud Platform (fully compatible) * Splunk Enterprise 9.3 and 10.x * Python Runtime: Fully optimized for Python 3.9 through Python 3.13 runtimes. * Upgrade Path: Safely replaces older Splunk Add-on Builder (AoB) versions of this TA. Your existing modular inputs and account configurations will carry over seamlessly.


Description:
The SailPoint Adaptive Response add-on allows Splunk administrators to automate security governance actions, such as revoking access from an enterprise user, using the powerful provisioning engine found in IdentityIQ. Automation begins when Splunk detects an alert and initiates a web-service request to one or more of a dozen action-specific endpoints available in SailPoint IdentityIQ after configuration. SailPoint IdentityIQ then creates, prioritizes, and processes the alert(s). The add-on also provides a way to retrieve all task results within Splunk®. It utilizes IdentityIQ API built upon the RESTful SCIM2.0 to achieve this. Along with the custom alert actions, the SailPoint Adaptive Response Add-on also provides two (3) new source types with in Splunk®. SailPoint Syslog Events: Used to collect Syslog events from IdentityIQ SailPoint Audit Events: Used to collect Audit events from IdentityIQ SailPoint Task Results: Used to collect Task results from IdentityIQ Users can configure these source type to collect events to Splunk® and populate a custom dashboard visualizing different types and details for these events.

Old "field" \= the base64-cell `key` in the 1.x table-API response; new "field" \= the JSON key in the 2.0 External API response. Everything here was confirmed directly against source (Go mappers, proto/OpenAPI spec, and the ClickHouse/Postgres view definitions backing each endpoint) — nothing is guessed. ## Cross-cutting changes (all 6 inputs) * **Transport**: `PUT` with a JSON `getTableRequest` body → `GET` with query params (`startIndex`, `count`, `filters`, `sortBy`, `sortOrder`). * **Response envelope**: `getTableResponse.data.rows[].cells[{key,value}]` (base64-encoded values, decode required) → plain JSON objects, camelCase keys, no encoding. `totalNumberOfResults` (separate `/count` call, only on accounts/discovery/identities/system\_logs) → `totalResults`/`itemsPerPage` returned inline on every page (no separate count call needed). * **Pagination**: posture/alerts previously fetched a single page capped at `limit` with no next-page handling — results beyond `limit` in one poll were silently dropped. accounts/discovery/identities/system\_logs already paginated fully. **2.0 pages through all results on every input** — this is a behavior change for posture/alerts specifically (fixes a latent data loss bug; `limit` now controls page size, not a hard cap). * **Enums**: raw integer codes (e.g. `status=5`, `risk_level=30`) → string enum names (e.g. `checkStatus="ALERT_STATUS_TO_REVIEW"`, `severity="HIGH"`). item.description:

Release Notes:
1.0.0 — First general-availability release Deploy an AWS Lambda into your own AWS account, entirely from the Splunk UI, that streams S3 objects into Splunk over HEC: S3 ObjectCreated -> Lambda -> HEC -> index. Deployment runs in-process against the AWS API (boto3) - no AWS console, no AWS CLI. AWS credentials are stored encrypted in Splunk and can be wiped automatically once the Lambda is created. Nothing in the add-on or the deployed Lambda ever calls the vendor: license verification is fully offline. WHAT'S INCLUDED \- One-click deploy of the ingest Lambda (IAM role, function, reserved concurrency, S3 ObjectCreated notification). Preview shows the exact AWS calls before anything is created. \- Compression auto-detected from content, not from the file name: gzip, zstd, bzip2 or uncompressed. Everything is streamed, so memory does not grow with object size. \- Object layout auto-detected: \* line-oriented - NDJSON, syslog, CSV, ALB / CloudFront / VPC Flow Logs, S3 access logs. One line per event; no line is dropped. \* JSON envelope {"Records":\[...]} - CloudTrail, AWS Config, GuardDuty - and bare JSON arrays. One event per element, streamed element by element. \- Routing table: map key prefixes to their own index and sourcetype (longest prefix wins), so one deployment feeds many log types. A route can post to HEC /raw so the sourcetypes the Splunk Add-on for AWS already ships do the line breaking and field extraction, and can skip a header line (VPC Flow Logs). \- Recovery from a lapsed subscription: objects refused while the license is expired are recorded, and "Recover missed objects" replays exactly those objects after renewal - no duplicates. \- Air-gapped support: corporate proxy for AWS API egress, and an exportable self-contained deploy script (Lambda binary embedded) for Splunk hosts with no AWS connectivity. \- Hourly license\_status events (sourcetype s3\_lambda\_deployer:license) so you can alert on expiry with your own saved searches. REQUIREMENTS \- A valid license key (this is a paid add-on). Enter it on the Licensing tab. Keys are node-locked to your AWS account id. \- Splunk Enterprise / Splunk Cloud with an enabled HEC endpoint reachable from AWS Lambda, and a token whose allowed indexes cover your target index. \- AWS credentials with permission to create the IAM role, Lambda function and bucket notification. They are needed only at deploy time - the deployed Lambda runs on its own IAM role. KNOWN LIMITATION \- If the license stays expired longer than your S3 bucket's retention / lifecycle period, AWS deletes those objects and that data cannot be recovered into Splunk. Align your renewal with the bucket lifecycle. Support: [support@innosw.net](mailto:support@innosw.net)


Short Description:
Deploy a serverless S3-to-Splunk pipeline into your own AWS account, right from the Splunk UI. An event-driven Go Lambda streams and gunzips new S3 objects to your HEC endpoint in real time — no Heavy Forwarder, no polling, no idle infrastructure. Works on Splunk Cloud and Enterprise.


Description:
Inno Streaming Add-on for AWS S3 lets a Splunk administrator deploy a serverless ingestion pipeline into their own AWS account directly from the Splunk UI — no AWS console, no aws CLI, and no forwarder in the data path. The problem: getting S3 data into Splunk usually means standing up and maintaining polling-based inputs or Heavy Forwarders, granting broad AWS access, and paying for idle infrastructure. This add-on replaces that with an event-driven, in-account design. How it works: you enter your AWS credentials (stored encrypted in Splunk), your HEC endpoint, target index, and S3 bucket, then click Deploy. Using the AWS API (boto3), the add-on provisions a least-privilege IAM role, a compiled Go Lambda, and an S3 ObjectCreated notification. From then on, every object that lands in the bucket triggers the Lambda, which streams and decompresses the object and forwards the records to your Splunk HEC endpoint in real time. Data flows S3 → Lambda → HEC entirely inside your AWS account; it never passes through the vendor. Highlights: - Deploy from the Splunk UI in minutes; idempotent re-deploys. - Event-driven and serverless — the Lambda scales with your data and back to zero when idle. - Installs on Splunk Cloud search heads and on Splunk Enterprise / Heavy Forwarders. - AWS keys are only needed at deploy time and are auto-wiped after a successful deploy; the Lambda runs on its own IAM role. - Compression auto-detected from the content, not the file name: gzip, zstd, bzip2 or uncompressed — all streamed, so memory does not grow with object size. - Two object layouts, auto-detected: * line-oriented — NDJSON / JSON Lines and plain-text logs (syslog, CSV, key=value, ALB / CloudFront access logs, VPC Flow Logs, S3 access logs). One line, one event. * JSON envelope {"Records":[...]} and bare JSON arrays — CloudTrail, AWS Config, GuardDuty. One event per element, streamed element by element, so a CloudTrail file with 100k records never lands in memory at once. - Routing table: map key prefixes to their own index and sourcetype, so one deployment feeds many log types. A route can post to HEC /raw and reuse the sourcetypes the Splunk Add-on for AWS already ships for line breaking and field extraction. - Compiled Go Lambda binary, corporate-proxy support, and an air-gapped export option for Splunk hosts with no AWS connectivity. Requires an HEC endpoint reachable from AWS Lambda and a token whose allowed indexes cover your target index. The add-on is free to install. A license key is required to preview, export or deploy; keys are node-locked to your AWS account id and verified entirely offline. See detailed performance-benchmark results (measured S3-to-HEC throughput and tuning), step-by-step usage guides, full documentation, and licensing at https://innosw.net - 11 USD / month - 110 USD / year

No change to supported versions - the app still targets Splunk Enterprise 9.1 through 10.x, search heads only, and python.required is ignored below 10.2. Write path fixes: * Settings and record writes now use the correct splunkd request transport and KV Store upsert semantics, so first-time writes (including the initial settings save on a fresh install) succeed. * \- The app REST endpoint is now exposed at all nested route depths, so the full change workflow (validate, approve, publish, roll back) resolves through Splunk Web. * \- Request bodies are delivered reliably through Splunk Web's proxy. * \- The audit hash-chain tip is resolved deterministically, independent of KV Store sort ordering. Install and first-use fixes: * Removed a setup gate that could leave a fresh install unable to reach the app views. The Setup page remains available from the navigation bar. * \- A brand-new lookup with no existing baseline now diffs cleanly instead of surfacing a raw splunkd error. Validated on Splunk Enterprise 9.4 with KV Store; AppInspect clean. Requires a Splunk restart after install to register the REST handler and KV Store collections.


Short Description:
Air-gap-first governance for Splunk lookup changes: inventory, deterministic validation, semantic diff, approvals with separation of duties, verified publication and rollback, audit evidence export, offline transfer bundles, and optional behind-the-firewall AI review with zero authority. No cloud dependencies. No telemetry.


Description:
Federal AI LookupOps turns Splunk lookup edits into governed changes. It is built air-gap-first: no cloud dependencies, no external services, and no telemetry. Analysts propose candidate changes by uploading a CSV, pasting records, or cloning the current lookup. A deterministic policy engine validates schemas, unique and composite keys, field types (IPv4, IPv6, CIDR, hostname, URL, email, date, boolean, number), enumerations, patterns, blank values, duplicates, and expirations. A key-aware semantic diff shows exactly what will change - additions, removals, field-level modifications, normalization-only changes, and schema changes - each with a stable evidence ID. Approvers act under enforced separation of duties; self-approval is blocked server-side. Publication captures the production content hash at submission, re-verifies it immediately before the write, publishes only through documented Splunk interfaces, verifies the resulting hash after the write, and preserves the previous version for one-action verified rollback. Every step lands in a hash-chained audit trail with an exportable JSON evidence report. Deterministic offline bundles with SHA-256 manifests move changes safely between enclaves. Optionally, connect a customer-approved, behind-the-firewall LLM (OpenAI-compatible, Ollama, or custom JSON). AI review runs server-side only with TLS verification always enforced, and provides risk assessment, justification-vs-diff contradiction detection, reviewer questions, policy proposals, normalization patches, dependency impact, and release narratives. Every material AI finding must cite deterministic evidence IDs, and the model has zero authority - it can never approve, publish, or roll back. Works with your existing SAML login through Splunk's own authentication. Includes role-based capabilities (view, submit, approve, publish, rollback, AI use, AI admin), KV Store-backed state that replicates across search-head clusters, and full documentation. Release Notes:
**Version 0.9.0 (July 22nd, 2026)** - **IMPORTANT / BREAKING CHANGE:** The Oracle SBC media-flow fields have been renamed to align with Oracle's own terminology. The old "west", "east", "extra_west" and "extra_east" field-name prefixes were a nonstandard naming scheme that did not appear anywhere in Oracle's documentation. The new names map to Oracle's flow-set and flow-direction concepts — Flow-Set 1 or 2 (fs1 / fs2), and Forward or Reverse (fwd / rev). For the media flow and quality-of-service fields the mapping is: - `west_*` → `fs1_fwd_*` (Flow-Set 1, Forward direction) - `east_*` → `fs1_rev_*` (Flow-Set 1, Reverse direction) - `extra_*` → `fs2_fwd_*` / `fs2_rev_*` (Flow-Set 2, Forward / Reverse) A few groups of fields do not follow that prefix pattern exactly: the media-stop-time and RTP transmitted-byte/packet counters are indexed by flow-set and calling/called party, and the session R-Factor and MOS values are now simply `calling_r_factor`, `calling_mos`, `called_r_factor` and `called_mos` (they are session-level, not per-flow). If you have built any of your own saved searches, dashboards, or reports that reference the old field names, you will need to update them when you upgrade. - Added a new search command, `| checksbcflowfieldnames`, to make that migration easy and exact. Run it (as an admin, or as a user with the `admin_all_objects` capability, for a complete picture) and it will itemize every place in your Splunk knowledge objects, ie saved searches, dashboards, macros, event types, data models, etc, that still reference any old field name, giving you the precise new name to use for each one. - Call detail view for Oracle SBC calls now includes a single-row summary table at the top echoing top level details like ingress/egress realm, time, disposition and duration etc. - Call detail view for Oracle SBC calls now includes a CallFlowGraph module that presents a DAG visualization of the various ip addresses and ingress/egress realms involved in the B2BUA signaling and media flow.

item.description:

Release Notes:
**⚠️ Critical bug fix. Recommended upgrade for anyone running v1.0.2 through v1.0.5.** ## The bug `advance_ts` used a `strptime` call with a hard-coded `.%f` format directive, which raises `ValueError` when the WithSecure Elements API returns a timestamp without fractional seconds. Both forms are valid ISO 8601 and both are returned by the API depending on the event: ``` 2026-07-22T11:19:08.804Z ← parsed correctly 2026-07-22T11:19:08Z ← ValueError ! ``` The exception was raised inside `_set_checkpoint`, so the polling cursor never advanced past that timestamp. Every subsequent polling cycle re-fetched the same window and re-indexed the same events, producing an ever-growing pile of duplicates in the target index. ## Who is affected * The bug has existed since **v1.0.2 (June 2026)**. Every version from v1.0.2 to v1.0.5 is affected. * It only manifests when the **last event of a fetched batch** happens to have no fractional seconds — which is why it was not caught earlier in testing. About one third of the events in the reporter's environment turned out to be in that form. * **Symptom**: continuously growing duplicate ingestion for `withsecure:epp:security_event`, `withsecure:epp:bcd_incident`, and/or `withsecure:epp:bcd_detection`. ## The fix * New helper `parse_iso_utc` in `withsecure_api.py` uses `datetime.fromisoformat` after rewriting the trailing `Z` as `+00:00`. Handles both timestamp forms natively on Python 3.9+. * `parse_iso_utc` also normalises the result to a **timezone-aware UTC** datetime, so any downstream arithmetic or formatting is unambiguous even if a future API revision were to return a non-UTC offset. * `utc_iso` now converts a tz-aware input to UTC before formatting, so the trailing literal `Z` always reflects the actual UTC instant. * `advance_ts` (`withsecure_api.py`) and `_parse_iso` (`withsecure_locks.py`) both use the new helper — a single source of truth for ISO 8601 parsing across the add-on. ## What to do after upgrading If you were affected by duplicates on a previous version, the duplicates already in the index remain (Splunk does not rewrite past events). New events indexed after v1.0.6 will be clean. To de-duplicate at search time until historical events roll off retention: ``` index=main sourcetype="withsecure:epp:security_event" | dedup id sortby -_time ``` Similar patterns for `withsecure:epp:bcd_incident` (`dedup incidentId,updatedTimestamp`) and `withsecure:epp:bcd_detection` (`dedup detectionId`). ## Upgrade safety Non-destructive in-place upgrade when installed via Splunk's standard "Install app from file → Upgrade app" workflow (or `splunk install app -update 1`): * existing KV Store checkpoints are preserved → polling picks up right where it left off, no historical re-fetch * existing input configuration in `local/inputs.conf` (credentials, intervals, filters, proxy settings) is preserved * no scheme or config changes → no user action required ## Compatibility * Splunk Enterprise / Cloud: **9.0, 9.1, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4, 10.0, 10.1, 10.2, 10.3, 10.4, 10.5** * CIM: 4.x, 5.x, 6.x, 8.x * Python: 3.9+ * Splunk KV Store: enabled


Short Description:

Description:
The WithSecure Elements Add-on collects endpoint protection and detection data from the WithSecure Elements API. It ingests EPP Security Events and EDR Broad Context Detections through OAuth2-authenticated modular inputs, enabling centralized security event analysis in Splunk. The add-on maps collected events to CIM endpoint, malware, intrusion detection, and process tags, facilitating correlation with other security data sources. Two modular inputs handle data collection: withsecure_epp_input retrieves endpoint protection events, while withsecure_bcd_input collects EDR broad context detection incidents. Short Description:
Build, import, validate, and package Splunk add-ons through a visual browser UI — no CLI. Create inputs (REST/shell/Python), alert actions, source types, field extractions, CIM mappings, lookups, and setup pages on the UCC Framework, run inputs and alerts in the browser to inspect their output, validate with AppInspect, and package for Splunkbase in one click.


Description:
TA Studio is a browser-based visual workbench for building Splunk® add-ons (TAs) on the Universal Configuration Console (UCC) Framework — without touching the command line. Authoring a quality add-on normally means working with the ucc-gen CLI, hand-editing globalConfig.json and a web of .conf files, and running AppInspect and packaging from a terminal. TA Studio replaces that workflow with a guided, point-and-click interface that runs entirely inside your own Splunk instance. From one UI you can create and manage data inputs (REST API, shell command, or Python modular inputs), alert actions (including Enterprise Security adaptive response), source types, field extractions with a live regex builder, CIM data model mappings, setup pages (accounts, proxy, logging), CSV lookups, and event types. You can import existing Splunk Add-on Builder and conf-based add-ons to modernize them, run inputs and alert actions right in the browser to inspect the events and output they produce, validate with AppInspect (including cloud checks) and review the results, then package a Splunkbase-ready archive in one click. TA Studio also includes built-in AI assistance to help you generate and refine input and alert-action code as you work. It otherwise runs entirely within your local Splunk environment: your add-on projects are not collected, transmitted, or stored outside your instance, and AI features send only the content you choose to submit to your selected AI provider.
